source_refs.note: Exercise 14.3, Question 2 (i)-(iv): unit vector perpendicular to the plane of a and b, and sin of the angle, via a x b (book p.282). Answer key PDF 312 (gives the + unit vector only).

blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Find a unit vector perpendicular to the plane containing \(\underline{a}\) and \(\underline{b}\). Also find sine of the angle between them: \(\underline{a} = \underline{i} + 6\underline{j} - 3\underline{k}\), \(\underline{b} = 2\underline{i} + \underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\).
blocks.explanation:
A unit normal and angle question.
We must find a unit vector perpendicular to both \(\underline{a}\) and \(\underline{b}\), and \(\sin\theta\).
Plan: \(\underline{a} \times \underline{b}\), divide by its length; then \(\sin\theta = |\underline{a} \times \underline{b}|/(|\underline{a}||\underline{b}|)\).
steps:
Given: \(\underline{a} = \underline{i} + 6\underline{j} - 3\underline{k}\), \(\underline{b} = 2\underline{i} + \underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\).
To find: a unit vector \(\hat{n}\) perpendicular to the plane of \(\underline{a}\) and \(\underline{b}\), and \(\sin\theta\).
Method: \(\underline{a} \times \underline{b}\) is perpendicular to both vectors, so to their plane; dividing it by its length gives a unit vector. From \(|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}| = |\underline{a}||\underline{b}|\sin\theta\) we get \(\sin\theta\).

Write the determinant
\[\underline{a} \times \underline{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \underline{i} & \underline{j} & \underline{k} \\ 1 & 6 & -3 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Row 1 holds the unit vectors, row 2 the components of the first vector \(\underline{a}\), row 3 those of the second \(\underline{b}\). The order of the rows follows the order of the product.

Work out the three minors
\[\underline{i}\text{ minor} = (6)(3) - (-3)(1) = 21\]
\[\underline{j}\text{ minor} = (1)(3) - (-3)(2) = 9\]
\[\underline{k}\text{ minor} = (1)(1) - (6)(2) = -11\]
Why: For each unit vector cover its row and column; the minor is (top-left)(bottom-right) minus (top-right)(bottom-left).

Attach the signs \(+, -, +\)
\[\underline{a} \times \underline{b} = \underline{i}(21) - \underline{j}(9) + \underline{k}(-11)\]
\[= 21\underline{i} - 9\underline{j} - 11\underline{k}\]
Why: Expanding a determinant along row 1 uses the sign pattern \(+, -, +\); the middle (\(\underline{j}\)) term is subtracted.

Length of \(\underline{a} \times \underline{b}\)
\[|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}| = \sqrt{(21)^2 + (-9)^2 + (-11)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{643}\]
Why: Length of \(x\underline{i} + y\underline{j} + z\underline{k}\) is \(\sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2}\).

Unit vector perpendicular to the plane
\[\hat{n} = \pm\dfrac{\underline{a} \times \underline{b}}{|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}|}\]
\[= \pm\dfrac{21\underline{i} - 9\underline{j} - 11\underline{k}}{\sqrt{643}}\]
Why: Dividing a vector by its own length keeps its direction and makes its length 1. The opposite vector is also perpendicular to the plane, so there are two answers, \(\pm\).

Lengths of \(\underline{a}\) and \(\underline{b}\)
\[|\underline{a}| = \sqrt{(1)^2 + (6)^2 + (-3)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{46}\]
\[|\underline{b}| = \sqrt{(2)^2 + (1)^2 + (3)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{14}\]
Why: Needed in the denominator of \(\sin\theta\).

Sine of the angle
\[\sin\theta = \dfrac{|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}|}{|\underline{a}|\,|\underline{b}|}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{643}}{\sqrt{46}\,\sqrt{14}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{643}}{\sqrt{644}}\]
Why: From \(|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}| = |\underline{a}||\underline{b}|\sin\theta\). Since \(0 \le \theta \le \pi\), \(\sin\theta \ge 0\), so only the positive value.

Check: \(\hat{n}\) is perpendicular to \(\underline{a}\)
\[\underline{a} \cdot (\underline{a} \times \underline{b}) = (1)(21) + (6)(-9) + (-3)(-11)\]
\[= 21 - 54 + 33 = 0\]
Why: A zero dot product confirms the direction (the same works for \(\underline{b}\)).

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Find a unit vector perpendicular to the plane containing \(\underline{a}\) and \(\underline{b}\). Also find sine of the angle between them: \(\underline{a} = -\underline{i} - \underline{j} - \underline{k}\), \(\underline{b} = 2\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 4\underline{k}\).
blocks.explanation:
A unit normal and angle question.
We must find a unit vector perpendicular to both \(\underline{a}\) and \(\underline{b}\), and \(\sin\theta\).
Plan: \(\underline{a} \times \underline{b}\), divide by its length; then \(\sin\theta = |\underline{a} \times \underline{b}|/(|\underline{a}||\underline{b}|)\).
steps:
Given: \(\underline{a} = -\underline{i} - \underline{j} - \underline{k}\), \(\underline{b} = 2\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 4\underline{k}\).
To find: a unit vector \(\hat{n}\) perpendicular to the plane of \(\underline{a}\) and \(\underline{b}\), and \(\sin\theta\).
Method: \(\underline{a} \times \underline{b}\) is perpendicular to both vectors, so to their plane; dividing it by its length gives a unit vector. From \(|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}| = |\underline{a}||\underline{b}|\sin\theta\) we get \(\sin\theta\).

Write the determinant
\[\underline{a} \times \underline{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \underline{i} & \underline{j} & \underline{k} \\ -1 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & -3 & 4 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Row 1 holds the unit vectors, row 2 the components of the first vector \(\underline{a}\), row 3 those of the second \(\underline{b}\). The order of the rows follows the order of the product.

Work out the three minors
\[\underline{i}\text{ minor} = (-1)(4) - (-1)(-3) = -7\]
\[\underline{j}\text{ minor} = (-1)(4) - (-1)(2) = -2\]
\[\underline{k}\text{ minor} = (-1)(-3) - (-1)(2) = 5\]
Why: For each unit vector cover its row and column; the minor is (top-left)(bottom-right) minus (top-right)(bottom-left).

Attach the signs \(+, -, +\)
\[\underline{a} \times \underline{b} = \underline{i}(-7) - \underline{j}(-2) + \underline{k}(5)\]
\[= -7\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\]
Why: Expanding a determinant along row 1 uses the sign pattern \(+, -, +\); the middle (\(\underline{j}\)) term is subtracted.

Length of \(\underline{a} \times \underline{b}\)
\[|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}| = \sqrt{(-7)^2 + (2)^2 + (5)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{78}\]
Why: Length of \(x\underline{i} + y\underline{j} + z\underline{k}\) is \(\sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2}\).

Unit vector perpendicular to the plane
\[\hat{n} = \pm\dfrac{\underline{a} \times \underline{b}}{|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}|}\]
\[= \pm\dfrac{-7\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}}{\sqrt{78}}\]
Why: Dividing a vector by its own length keeps its direction and makes its length 1. The opposite vector is also perpendicular to the plane, so there are two answers, \(\pm\).

Lengths of \(\underline{a}\) and \(\underline{b}\)
\[|\underline{a}| = \sqrt{(-1)^2 + (-1)^2 + (-1)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{3}\]
\[|\underline{b}| = \sqrt{(2)^2 + (-3)^2 + (4)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{29}\]
Why: Needed in the denominator of \(\sin\theta\).

Sine of the angle
\[\sin\theta = \dfrac{|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}|}{|\underline{a}|\,|\underline{b}|}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{78}}{\sqrt{3}\,\sqrt{29}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{78}}{\sqrt{87}}\]
Why: From \(|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}| = |\underline{a}||\underline{b}|\sin\theta\). Since \(0 \le \theta \le \pi\), \(\sin\theta \ge 0\), so only the positive value.

Check: \(\hat{n}\) is perpendicular to \(\underline{a}\)
\[\underline{a} \cdot (\underline{a} \times \underline{b}) = (-1)(-7) + (-1)(2) + (-1)(5)\]
\[= 7 - 2 - 5 = 0\]
Why: A zero dot product confirms the direction (the same works for \(\underline{b}\)).

blocks.prompt: 2 (iii) Find a unit vector perpendicular to the plane containing \(\underline{a}\) and \(\underline{b}\). Also find sine of the angle between them: \(\underline{a} = \underline{i} + \underline{j} + \underline{k}\), \(\underline{b} = \underline{i} - \underline{j} - \underline{k}\).
blocks.explanation:
A unit normal and angle question.
We must find a unit vector perpendicular to both \(\underline{a}\) and \(\underline{b}\), and \(\sin\theta\).
Plan: \(\underline{a} \times \underline{b}\), divide by its length; then \(\sin\theta = |\underline{a} \times \underline{b}|/(|\underline{a}||\underline{b}|)\).
steps:
Given: \(\underline{a} = \underline{i} + \underline{j} + \underline{k}\), \(\underline{b} = \underline{i} - \underline{j} - \underline{k}\).
To find: a unit vector \(\hat{n}\) perpendicular to the plane of \(\underline{a}\) and \(\underline{b}\), and \(\sin\theta\).
Method: \(\underline{a} \times \underline{b}\) is perpendicular to both vectors, so to their plane; dividing it by its length gives a unit vector. From \(|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}| = |\underline{a}||\underline{b}|\sin\theta\) we get \(\sin\theta\).

Write the determinant
\[\underline{a} \times \underline{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \underline{i} & \underline{j} & \underline{k} \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Row 1 holds the unit vectors, row 2 the components of the first vector \(\underline{a}\), row 3 those of the second \(\underline{b}\). The order of the rows follows the order of the product.

Work out the three minors
\[\underline{i}\text{ minor} = (1)(-1) - (1)(-1) = 0\]
\[\underline{j}\text{ minor} = (1)(-1) - (1)(1) = -2\]
\[\underline{k}\text{ minor} = (1)(-1) - (1)(1) = -2\]
Why: For each unit vector cover its row and column; the minor is (top-left)(bottom-right) minus (top-right)(bottom-left).

Attach the signs \(+, -, +\)
\[\underline{a} \times \underline{b} = \underline{i}(0) - \underline{j}(-2) + \underline{k}(-2)\]
\[= 2\underline{j} - 2\underline{k}\]
Why: Expanding a determinant along row 1 uses the sign pattern \(+, -, +\); the middle (\(\underline{j}\)) term is subtracted.

Length of \(\underline{a} \times \underline{b}\)
\[|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}| = \sqrt{(0)^2 + (2)^2 + (-2)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{8} = 2 \sqrt{2}\]
Why: Length of \(x\underline{i} + y\underline{j} + z\underline{k}\) is \(\sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2}\).

Unit vector perpendicular to the plane
\[\hat{n} = \pm\dfrac{\underline{a} \times \underline{b}}{|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}|}\]
\[= \pm\dfrac{2\underline{j} - 2\underline{k}}{2\sqrt{2}} = \pm\dfrac{\underline{j} - \underline{k}}{\sqrt{2}}\]
Why: Dividing a vector by its own length keeps its direction and makes its length 1. The opposite vector is also perpendicular to the plane, so there are two answers, \(\pm\).

Lengths of \(\underline{a}\) and \(\underline{b}\)
\[|\underline{a}| = \sqrt{(1)^2 + (1)^2 + (1)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{3}\]
\[|\underline{b}| = \sqrt{(1)^2 + (-1)^2 + (-1)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{3}\]
Why: Needed in the denominator of \(\sin\theta\).

Sine of the angle
\[\sin\theta = \dfrac{|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}|}{|\underline{a}|\,|\underline{b}|}\]
\[= \dfrac{2 \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}\,\sqrt{3}}\]
\[= \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}\]
Why: From \(|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}| = |\underline{a}||\underline{b}|\sin\theta\). Since \(0 \le \theta \le \pi\), \(\sin\theta \ge 0\), so only the positive value.

Check: \(\hat{n}\) is perpendicular to \(\underline{a}\)
\[\underline{a} \cdot (\underline{a} \times \underline{b}) = (1)(0) + (1)(2) + (1)(-2)\]
\[= 0 + 2 - 2 = 0\]
Why: A zero dot product confirms the direction (the same works for \(\underline{b}\)).

blocks.prompt: 2 (iv) Find a unit vector perpendicular to the plane containing \(\underline{a}\) and \(\underline{b}\). Also find sine of the angle between them: \(\underline{a} = 5\underline{i} + \underline{j} - 3\underline{k}\), \(\underline{b} = -2\underline{i} + 4\underline{j} + \underline{k}\).

steps:

\[\underline{k}\text{ minor} = (5)(4) - (1)(-2) = 22\]

Attach the signs \(+, -, +\)
\[\underline{a} \times \underline{b} = \underline{i}(13) - \underline{j}(-1) + \underline{k}(22)\]
\[= 13\underline{i} + \underline{j} + 22\underline{k}\]

\[\hat{n} = \pm\dfrac{\underline{a} \times \underline{b}}{|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}|}\]

\[|\underline{a}| = \sqrt{(5)^2 + (1)^2 + (-3)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{35}\]
\[|\underline{b}| = \sqrt{(-2)^2 + (4)^2 + (1)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{21}\]
Why: Needed in the denominator of \(\sin\theta\).

Sine of the angle
\[\sin\theta = \dfrac{|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}|}{|\underline{a}|\,|\underline{b}|}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{654}}{\sqrt{35}\,\sqrt{21}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{654}}{\sqrt{735}}\]
Why: From \(|\underline{a} \times \underline{b}| = |\underline{a}||\underline{b}|\sin\theta\). Since \(0 \le \theta \le \pi\), \(\sin\theta \ge 0\), so only the positive value.

Check: \(\hat{n}\) is perpendicular to \(\underline{a}\)
\[\underline{a} \cdot (\underline{a} \times \underline{b}) = (5)(13) + (1)(1) + (-3)(22)\]
\[= 65 + 1 - 66 = 0\]
Why: A zero dot product confirms the direction (the same works for \(\underline{b}\)).
